questions.q: Two objects are projected with same velocity $u$~however at different angles~$\alpha$ and $\beta$~with the horizontal. If $\alpha + \beta = 90 °$, the ratio of horizontal range of the first object to the ${2}^{nd}$ object will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $\alpha + \beta = 90 °$

Range of the first projectile:

${R}_{1} = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2\alpha}{g}$

Range of the second projectile:

${R}_{2} = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2\beta}{g} = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin ( 180 ° - 2\alpha )}{g} = \dfrac{u^{2}\sin 2\alpha}{g}$

As we can see, both are equal.

${R}_{1} = {R}_{2}$

Therefore,

${R}_{1}: {R}_{2} = 1: 1$

questions.q: At time $t = 0$~a particle starts travelling from a height $7\overset{^}{z}cm$ in a plane keeping $z$ coordinate constant. At any instant of time, it's position along the $x$ and $y$ directions are defined as $3t$ and $5t^{3}$ respectively. At $t = 1s$ acceleration of the particle will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The position vector of the particle can be written as,

$\overset{→}{r} = 3t\overset{^}{i} + 5t^{3}\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

The velocity of the particle will be,~

$\overset{→}{v} = \dfrac{d \overset{→}{r}}{d t} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 15t^{2}\overset{^}{j}$

Now the acceleration of the particle will be,

$\overset{→}{a} = \dfrac{d \overset{→}{v}}{d t} = \dfrac{d^{2}\overset{→}{r}}{dt^{2}} = 30t\overset{^}{j}$

At $t = 1s ⇒ \dfrac{d^{2}r}{dt^{2}} = 30\overset{^}{j}$

questions.q:
The co-ordinates of a particle moving in $x-y$ plane are given by : $x=2+4 \mathrm{t}, y=3 \mathrm{t}+8 \mathrm{t}^2$.
The motion of the particle is :
options: uniformly accelerated having motion along a parabolic path.
uniform motion along a straight line.
uniformly accelerated having motion along a straight line.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & x=2+4 t \\ & \frac{d x}{d t}=v_x=4 \\ & \frac{d v_x}{d t}=a_x=0 \\ & y=3 t+8 t^2 \\ & \frac{d y}{d t}=v_y=3+16 t \\ & \frac{d v_y}{d t}=a_y=16 \end{aligned}$ the motion will be uniformly accelerated motion. For path $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}=2+4 \mathrm{t} \\ & \frac{(\mathrm{x}-2)}{4}=\mathrm{t} \end{aligned}$
Put this value of $t$ is equation of $yy=3\left(\frac{x-2}{4}\right)+8\left(\frac{x-2}{4}\right)^2$ this is a quadratic equation so path will be parabola.

questions.q: A particle moves such that its position vector $\overset{→}{r}\left(t\right) = cos  \omegat\overset{^}{i} + sin  \omegat\overset{^}{j}$ where $\omega$ is a constant and $t$ is time. Then which of the following statements is true for the velocity $\overset{→}{v}  \left(t\right)$ and acceleration $\overset{→}{a}  \left(t\right)$ of the particle:
options: $\overset{→}{v}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{r}$ and $\overset{→}{a}$ is directed away from the origin
$\overset{→}{v}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{r}$ and $\overset{→}{a}$ is directed towards the origin
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{r} = cos \omegat\overset{^}{i} + sin \omegat\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{→}{v} = \dfrac{d\overset{→}{r}}{dt} = \omega \left(-sin \omegat\overset{^}{i} + cos \omegat\overset{^}{j}\right)$
$\overset{→}{a} = $\dfrac{d\overset{→}{v}}{dt} = - {\omega}^{2} \left(cos \omegat\overset{^}{i} + sin \omegat\overset{^}{j}\right)$
$\overset{→}{a} = - {\omega}^{2}\overset{→}{r} ∴ \overset{→}{a}$ is antiparallel to $\overset{→}{r}$
$\overset{→}{v} . \overset{→}{r} = \omega\left(- sin \omega tcos \omegat + cos \omega tsin \omegat\right) = 0$
So $\overset{→}{v} ⊥ \overset{→}{r}

questions.q: A projectile is projected at $30 °$ from horizontal with initial velocity $40ms^{- 1}$. The velocity of the projectile at $t = 2s$ from the start will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that& $v = 40ms^{- 1}$.

The components of the velocity will be~${v}_{y} = vsin30 ° = \dfrac{40ms^{- 1}}{2} = 20ms^{- 1}{v}_{x} = vcos30 ° = \dfrac{40\sqrt{3}}{2}ms^{- 1} = 20\sqrt{3}ms^{- 1}$

The time taken to reach maximum height is~$T = \dfrac{usin30 °}{g} = \dfrac{20ms^{- 1}}{10ms^{- 2}} = 2s$

Hence, at~$T = 2s, \text{as}{v}_{y} = 0ms^{- 1}\text{therefore}{v}_{net} = {v}_{x} = 20\sqrt{3}ms^{- 1}$.

questions.q: Motion of a particle in $x - y$~plane is described by a set of following equations $x = 4\sin \left(\dfrac{π}{2} - \omegat\right)m$ and $y = 4\sin \left(\omegat\right)m$. The path of the particle will be

questions.solution:
$x = 4\sin \left(\dfrac{π}{2} - \omegat\right) =$=4\cos \left(\omegat\right),

$y = 4\sin \left(\omegat\right)

Clearly,~ ~$x^{2} + y^{2} = $\l$left(4\cos \left(\omegat\right))$2 + $\l$left(4\sin \left(\omegat\right))$2 ⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} = 16$

Hence, the path covered by particle is a circle.

$

questions.q: A butterfly is flying with a velocity $4\sqrt{2}ms^{- 1}$ in north-east direction. Wind is slowly blowing at $1ms^{- 1}$ from north to south. The resultant displacement of the butterfly in $3$ seconds is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{V}BW = 4\sqrt{2}\cos 4 5\overset{^}{i} + 4\sqrt{2}\sin 4 5\overset{^}{j}$
$= 4\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{→}{V}w = - \overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{→}{V}B = \overset{→}{V}BW + \overset{→}{V}w = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{→}{S}B = \overset{→}{V}B \times t = ( 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} ) \times 3 = 12\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j}$
\left|\overset{→}{S}B\right| = \sqrt{( 12{)}^{2} + ( 9{)}^{2}} = 15m$

$

questions.q: A particle moving in a circle of radius $R$ with uniform speed takes time $T$ to complete one revolution. If this particle is projected with the same speed at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it is equal to $4R$. The angle of projection $\theta$ is then given by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time period of circular motion is given by,

$\dfrac{2\piR}{v} = T ⇒ v = \dfrac{2\piR}{T}$

Now, maximum height $H = \dfrac{v^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$

$⇒ 4R = \dfrac{4{π}^{2}R^{2}}{T2}\dfrac{\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$

$⇒ sin\theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{2gT^{2}}{{π}^{2}R}}$

$⇒ \theta = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2gT^{2}}{{π}^{2}R}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: An object moves at a constant speed along a circular path in a horizontal plane with centre at the origin. When the object is at $x = + 2m$, its velocity is $- 4\overset{^}{j}ms^{- 1}$ . The object’s velocity $( v )$ and acceleration $( a )$ at $x = – 2m$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: As the speed is constant, only centripetal acceleration will act(towards the centre of the circular path),& ${a}_{c} = \dfrac{v2}{r} = \dfrac{42}{2} = 8ms^{- 2}$~towards the centre which at the given time will be towards right, hence~$\overset{→}{a}c = 8\overset{^}{i}ms^{- 2}$. Velocity of the particle at this instant will in upward direction and hence~$\overset{→}{v} = 4\overset{^}{j}ms^{- 1}$.

questions.q: A helicopter is flying horizontally with a speed $v$ at an altitude $h$& has to drop a food packet for a man on the ground. What is the distance of helicopter from the man when the food packet is dropped ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The aeroplane imparts $v$ velocity to the food packet horizontally when dropping. Horizontal range of food packet $= v \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$
Also, Horizontal distance, travelled by aeroplane $= v \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$ thus, vertical distance between aeroplane and person $= h$
distance $= \sqrt{\dfrac{2v^{2}h}{g} + h^{2}}$

questions.q:
If the angular velocity of earth's spin is increased such that the bodies at the equator start floating, the duration of the day would be approximately :
(Take : $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$,~the radius of earth, $R = 6400 \times {10}^{3}m$, Take $\pi = 3 . 14$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For objects to float,&

$mg = m{ω}^{2}R$

$\omega =$ angular velocity of the earth.

$R =$ Radius of earth

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{R}} . . . \left(1\right)$

Duration of day $= T$

$T = $\dfrac{2\pi}{ω} . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ T = 2\$pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R}{g}}

$= 2\$pi\sqrt{\dfrac{6400 \times {10}^{3}}{10}}

$⇒ $\dfrac{T}{60} =$83 . 775$~minutes

$≃ 84$ \text{ and } minutes

$

questions.q: In a car race on straight road, car $A$ takes a time $t$ less than car $B$ at the finish and passes finishing point with a speed $v$~more than that of car $B .$ Both the cars start from rest and travel with constant acceleration ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ ~respectively. Then $v$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,&
Initially both car is at rest, so& ${u}_{1} = {u}_{2} = 0$
Acceleration of car~$A \text{ and } B$~is~${a}_{1} \text{ and } {a}_{2}$

Let us assume,
Time of reach to destination of car~$A$~is,~${t}_{1} = {t}_{0}$
Time of reach to destination of car~$B$~is,~${t}_{2} = {t}_{0} + t$

Using second equation of motion, we have
${u}_{1}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{1}^{2} = {u}_{2}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{t2}^{2}$
$⇒ 0 \times t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{0}^{2} = 0 \times t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}\left({t}_{0} + t\right)2$
$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{a1}{a2}}{t}_{0} = {t}_{0} + t$
$⇒ {t}_{0} = \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{\dfrac{a1}{a2}} - 1}$

From first equation of motion, we have
$\begin{cases}{v}_{1} = {a}_{1}{t}_{0} & & {v}_{2} = {a}_{2}\left({t}_{0} + t\right)\end{cases}$
$⇒ v = {v}_{1} - {v}_{2} = \left({a}_{1} - {a}_{2}\right){t}_{0} - {a}_{2}t$
$⇒ v = \left({a}_{1} - {a}_{2}\right)\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{\dfrac{a1}{a2}} - 1} - {a}_{2}t$
$⇒ v = t\left(\dfrac{{a}_{1}\sqrt{{a}_{2}}}{{a}_{1} - {a}_{2}} - \dfrac{{a}_{2}{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1} - {a}_{2}} - {a}_{2}\right)$
$⇒ v = t \left(\dfrac{{a}_{1}\sqrt{{a}_{2}} - {a}_{2}{a}_{1}}{{a}_{1} - {a}_{2}}\right)
$⇒ v = $\sqrt{{a}_{1} . {a}_{2}}$t$

$

questions.q: A child stands on the edge of the cliff $10m$~above the ground and throws a stone horizontally with an initial speed of $5ms^{– 1}$ . Neglecting the air resistance, the speed with which the stone hits the ground will be _____ $ms^{– 1}$ (given, $g = 10ms^{– 2}$ ).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $u = 5ms^{- 1}, h = 10m$

Using~${v}_y^{2} = {u}_y^{2} + 2gh$~in vertical direction, we have the velocity of stone in vertical direction as~${v}_{y} = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{200}ms^{- 1}$~ ~(since,~${u}_{y} = 0$).

The final velocity along the horizontal direction is the same as the initial horizontal velocity as there is no acceleration along the x-axis.

The speed~with which the stone hits the ground is~

${v}_{net} = \sqrt{{v}_x^{2} + {v}_y^{2}} = \sqrt{25 + 200} = 15ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: If the radius of curvature of the path of two particles of same mass are in the ratio $3: 4$, then in order to have constant centripetal force, their velocities will be in the ratio of:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given ${m}_{1} = {m}_{2}$ and $\dfrac{r1}{r2} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

As centripetal force is given by $F = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$, in order to have the same centripetal force, we can write

${F}_{1} = {F}_{2} ⇒ \dfrac{{m}_{1}{v}_{1}^{2}}{r1} = \dfrac{{m}_{2}{v}_{2}^{2}}{r2} ⇒ \dfrac{v1}{v2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{r1}{r2}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q: The maximum height reached by a projectile is $64 \mathrm{~m}$. If the initial velocity is halved, the new maximum height of the projectile is _____ $\mathrm{m}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{H}_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{H}_{1 \text { max }}}{\mathrm{H}_{2 \max }}=\frac{\mathrm{u}_1^2}{\mathrm{u}_2^2} \\ & \frac{64}{\mathrm{H}_{2 \max }}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{(\mathrm{u} / 2)^2} \\ & \mathrm{H}_{2 \max }=16 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A stone tied to $180$ cm long string at its end is making $28$ revolutions in horizontal circle in every minute. The magnitude of acceleration of stone is~$\dfrac{1936}{x}ms^{- 2}$.~The value of $x$~______.

[Take~$\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular velocity,& $\omega = \dfrac{28 \times 2\pi}{60}rads^{- 1}$.

Required centripetal acceleration is given by,

$a = {ω}^{2}R$

$= \left(\dfrac{56}{60} \times \dfrac{22}{7}\right)2 \times 1 . 8$

$= \dfrac{( 44{)}^{2}}{225} \times 1 . 8 = \dfrac{1936}{125}$

Hence, required~$x = 125$.

questions.q: A fighter jet is flying horizontally at a certain altitude with a speed of $200\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. When it passes directly overhead an anti-aircraft gun, a bullet is fired from the gun, at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal, to hit the jet. If the bullet speed is $400ms^{- 1}$, the value of $\theta$ will be _____~$°$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In order to hit, horizontal velocity of both moving object should be same,

${V}_{1} = {V}_{2}cos\theta$~$⇒ 200 = 400cos\theta$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \theta = 60 °$
